and (1‐w) on asset Y is [ w ×D (X) + (1–w) ×D (Y) ]. 
 Institutions such as banks, pension funds and 
insurance companies are highly exposed to interest 
rate fluctuations. They would like to insure or 
i i it h fl t ti immunize against such fluctuations. 
 Solution: structure the balance sheet so that 
V(Assets) × D(Assets) = V(Liabilities) × D(Liabilities)V(Assets) × D(Assets) V(Liabilities) × D(Liabilities). 
 Continuous rebalancing is required for perfect 
immunization.

Example 3: true or false 
 Answer: Answer: 
o False. The term structure depends on the expected path 
of interest rates (among other factors). For example, if 
it t t td t fl l th t t t illinterest rates are expected to fall, the term structure will 
be downward sloping. 
o False. To minimize interest rate risks, we want 
MD(A) x V(A) – MD(L) x V(L) = 0. If V(A) > V(L), we want 
MD(A) < MD(L). That means we should invest in assets 
with shorter duration.with shorter duration.
